name: Decorator reflection is ordered and permission-filtered without transform handles

input.source_text: contract ClassDecorator { fun transform(declaration, arguments, context) } class First for ClassDecorator { public impl fun transform(d, a, c) -> Transformation { Transformation.empty } } class Second for ClassDecorator { public impl fun transform(d, a, c) -> Transformation { Transformation.empty } } @First(1, :two) @Second() class Box { } module M { public fun run() -> Object { let refused = try { Box.decorator_arguments.append([9]) } catch e { e }; [Box.decorators, Box.decorator_arguments, Box.decorator_phases, refused] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C094 exposes ordered decorator identity, ARGUMENTS and static/runtime phase participation as an immutable view. Only the identities were reported, and the arguments were stored as a Rust `{:?}` of the AST node, which could not read back as the value written; they are now recorded as the literal applied and reflected as ordered values. Phase participation is read from which C122 members the decorator Class actually declares. C094 forbids exposing mutable transform internals, so both views are readonly and a mutating selector answers ReadonlyMutationError, as `Box.methods` already did.
